text: Specialized motor carriers (automobile transporters, carriers of liquid and dry commodities in bulk, and movers of household goods) assert that they should be fully or partially exempted from the proposed regulations. The National Automobile Transporters Association (NATA) points out that the operating authority of automobile transporters is generally restricted to initial movements or secondary movements. The term initial movements means transportation of new motor vehicles from a place of manufacture or assembly specifically authorized to be served as a point of origin by the originating carrier's certificate or permit, to any point or place upon the authorized route or within its defined territory for delivery to a consignee or to a connecting carrier. The term secondary or subsequent movements means transportation of motor vehicles, except transportation of new motor vehicles from a place of manufacture or assembly, by a carrier to, from and between all points or places upon its authorized route or routes or within its authorized territory for delivery to a consignee or a connecting carrier. The NATA argues that zone expansion will affect automobile transporters holding secondary movement authority in much the same way as it will affect other types of carriers. Its primary concern is the effect expansion will have upon automobile transporters holding initial movement authority. Such authority is generally framed in such a way as to authorize a carrier to serve certain manufacturing or assembly plants of a named shipper.
